issue.title: Stop agent sync from resurrecting retired identities from immutable commit footers
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-ez.4 while hand-migrating the bob-cli bead and agent identities for epic sase-ez (plans:202608/revert_bead_reprefix_epic.md), and re-verified by sase-ez.land on 2026-08-03.

A full 'sase agent sync' infers agent pages for hoods it finds only in a repository's immutable commit history. When bob-cli's beads were reprefixed from gh_bobs-org__bob-cli-N to bob-cli-<base36>, the derived agent identities were renamed and the fourteen old bbugyi200.athena.gh_bobs-org__bob-cli-* bundle directories were retired from the agents sidecar. A subsequent full sync re-synthesized commit-only pages for those exact retired identities out of the primary repository's SASE_AGENT commit footers, which are published history and were deliberately left unchanged. sase-ez.4 had to run a second retirement pass to remove them again (agents sidecar commits 402e060 add, 8f4aada retire, 58ddd6f re-synthesize, 04fce79 retire again, in /home/bryan/.sase/projects/gh_bobs-org__bob-cli/repos/agents).

Impact: any identity rename is not durable. Every later full sync of that project re-creates the old pages, so a rename can only be held in place by repeated manual retirement. It also blocks safe cleanup of unrelated publication-queue residue in that project, because the cleanup path ('sase agent sync --drop-retired') runs a full sync and would resurrect the pages.

Scope: teach agent sync to remember retired or remapped identities (a durable tombstone or rename map consulted before commit-footer hood inference), so a commit-only page is not synthesized for an identity that has been retired or renamed. Cover the rename case, the plain-retirement case, and confirm a full sync after the fix leaves the sidecar unchanged. Do not rewrite commit footers; they are immutable published history.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-05: deprioritized and entangled with in-flight work, not fixed. This bead depends on active epic sase-ej (async sidecar publication), whose design is itself being reverted by active epic sase-fa ('Revert async sidecar publication so sase commit publishes sidecars inline again'), so the agent-sync publication path it targets is actively in motion. Confirming context: the gh_sase-org__sase publication outbox is currently fully quarantined, with the newest entries at HEAD 0e40decdc, which is sase-ej/sase-fa territory rather than this bead's. Reopen with a +1 once sase-fa lands if a retired or renamed identity still gets resurrected from SASE_AGENT commit footers by a full 'sase agent sync'.

payload.entry: Recorded for epic sase-fa's land phase (sase-fa.5): sase-fa (which reverts sase-ej's async sidecar publication) has now landed all of its phases, so the entanglement cited in this bead's 2026-08-05 backlog-triage cancellation ('this bead depends on active epic sase-ej ... whose design is itself being reverted by active epic sase-fa ... so the agent-sync publication path it targets is actively in motion') is resolved: sase-ej is closed and sase-fa is done moving the ground under this bead. Per scope decision 4 in plans:202608/revert_async_sidecar_publication.md, sase-fa deliberately does not run a full 'sase agent sync' against bob-cli, so the bob-cli identity-resurrection residue this bead describes is untouched and still real (bob-cli's outbox currently shows 9 quarantined / 2 retired agent-hood requests and 2 drifted hood-snapshot files, all pre-existing). This bead's own closing note invites a +1 'once sase-fa lands if a retired or renamed identity still gets resurrected from SASE_AGENT commit footers by a full sase agent sync' — that reproduction still requires actually running a full sync against bob-cli, which is out of scope here, so reopening is left to the owner rather than done unilaterally by this land phase.

evidence.note: Reproduced post sase-fa landing, as invited by this bead's 2026-08-05 close note. Ran a full 'sase agent sync --drop-retired --retry-quarantined -p bob-cli' from sase-fk (clearing the bob-cli publication outbox residue) at commit 10a0dff7ccfe5ec9340e1d6308e78d27df517b43 in the bob-cli agents sidecar. It re-synthesized commit-only pages for the previously-retired identities gh_bobs-org__bob-cli-2 (plus family members .1/.2/.3/.4 and a .land container) and gh_bobs-org__bob-cli-5 (plus member .5.5), which sase-ez.4 had retired twice before (agents sidecar commits 8f4aada/04fce79, referenced in this bead's description). Baseline before the sync: zero gh_bobs-org__bob-cli-* paths in the sidecar at HEAD fbc0688. The bug this bead describes is confirmed still present; sase-fk left the resurrected pages in place as reproduction evidence rather than re-retiring them, per its own instructions.
